title: Bound generic report request bodies before model binding
description: Stage 1 query/resource boundary gap verified in code: ReportConfigurationRules.MaxSerializedBytes limits normalized definitions only after binding, while the generic controller has no request size ceiling. Implement generic transport rejection, not a new business report. Existing Domain/Application models suffice; no persistence/schema changes or unrelated API changes. Preserve concurrent work, production boundaries and ERP permissions. Test only dedicated NEWERP_AutoAcceptance localdb target through process-only settings; no production, secrets/.env or deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Enforce a documented 512 KiB UTF-8 wire-body ceiling before JSON model binding for generic reporting POST/PUT routes, independent of Content-Length, including chunked input. Existing normalized 64 KiB definition limit remains separately enforced. Legitimate bounded create/update/import requests must remain accepted. Do not read an unbounded request into memory to implement the ceiling; use ASP.NET request limits and preserve authentication, current-user data scope, version checks and cancellation.

Return a bounded controlled 413 response for oversized report requests and a clear workspace input-too-large message; no echo of user payload, SQL or secrets and no persistence/preview/export work after rejection. Scope exception mapping to the report module; preserve unrelated middleware behavior and audit rejection rather than success. The wire limit must cover transfer envelope escaping and normal wrapper overhead without silently truncating definitions.

Add meaningful regression coverage for body limits on every reporting POST/PUT action family, normal boundary input, unknown-length body rejection, controlled module error mapping and client failure state. Run safe Release build/test, focused tests and scheduler self-test/contracts. Run actual HTTP oversized-body checks on the isolated local test API after its validated build is available; record genuine results and retain incomplete real browser/phase acceptance markers.
